analysis.investment_thesis: Belrise scores poorly on both Magic Formula metrics — Earnings Yield of ~4.7% (EBIT INR 1,021 Cr / EV ~INR 21,939 Cr) is well below the 6% minimum, and ROCE of 14.3% falls short of the 20%+ threshold for a high-quality business. At 39.6x P/E with negative FCF in 2025, the market is pricing in perfection for a thin-margin, capital-heavy auto parts supplier.
key_strengths: Revenue growing at 15.4% CAGR (2022-2025), showing consistent top-line expansion
Debt/Equity improved to 0.29 after apparent IPO equity raise in 2025 (equity doubled to INR 4,971 Cr)
Diversified product portfolio across 2W/3W/4W segments with some export exposure
key_risks: Capital intensity is extreme: FY25 capex of INR 868 Cr vs Net Profit of INR 355 Cr → FCF was -INR 163 Cr
Operating margins of 8.3% are thin, leaving little buffer against input cost inflation or demand slowdown
Finance costs growing at 12.4% CAGR (INR 307 Cr in FY25) consume ~30% of operating income
red_flags: Earnings Yield of ~4.7% — fails Magic Formula minimum of 6%; significantly overvalued on EBIT/EV basis
ROCE of 14.3% and ROE of 14.1% — both below Magic Formula's 20% quality threshold
FCF is deeply negative in 2025 (-INR 163 Cr) with capex exceeding 2.4x net profit — poor cash conversion
Net Profit CAGR (10.7%) lagging Revenue CAGR (15.4%) — operating leverage not materializing
analysis.detailed_analysis:
By the Magic Formula, Belrise fails on both axes simultaneously. Enterprise Value is approximately INR 21,939 Cr (Market Cap INR 19,052 Cr + Total Debt INR 2,964 Cr - Cash INR 77 Cr), giving an Earnings Yield (EBIT/EV) of just 4.7% — a red flag that screams overvaluation. ROCE of 14.3% confirms this is not a high-quality business; a great company earning 25%+ ROIC would at least justify a premium, but Belrise earns mediocre returns on a large and growing capital base. The P/E of 39.6x is simply unjustifiable for a business with 8.3% operating margins in a commoditized auto-components market.

The capital intensity story worsens on closer inspection. FY25 capex hit INR 868 Cr (vs. Net Profit of INR 355 Cr), producing negative FCF of -INR 163 Cr. Operating cash flow (INR 704 Cr) is decent, but it is being fully consumed by growth capex. Belrise appears to be in a "grow at all costs" mode funded by the 2025 equity raise; however, unless ROCE can push materially above the cost of capital (~14-15%+), this capital deployment destroys value rather than creating it. For a Magic Formula investor, this is a company to watch only after a significant price correction (EY needs to reach 12%+) or a sustained ROIC improvement above 20%.
